text.title: Multi-Region Failover Pattern Pack — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete warm-standby pack for a tier-1 payments API (RPO 5 / RTO 30, async PostgreSQL at 12 s lag, S3 with a cited backfill job, six dependencies with one bypass, a 5 percent live drill measuring RTO 22) with a note on each non-obvious value, then the pilot-light pack that says "zero data loss" and what the validator prints.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: payments-api runs in eu-west-1 with a read replica and replicated S3 bucket in eu-central-1. The product owner (product:maria) agreed RPO 5 minutes and RTO 30 minutes for tier-1. The architect (arch:alice) has to write down which pattern that buys, what it costs in standing capacity, and prove it with a drill before the quarterly review.

example.note: Warm standby is the cheapest pattern whose achievable RTO (22, measured) sits under the required 30; pilot light was costed at 60 minutes of scale-up and rejected (r-pattern-chosen-from-rpo-rto-and-cost). The secondary runs at 40 percent with a 12-minute scale-up inside the RTO, and `quotas_verified` is true because the quota request in `evidence[]` was approved (fm-07). The Route 53 record sits at 60 s but the drill measured 95 s of propagation, and the iOS SDK that caches IPs is listed with a client-side retry fallback (r-dns-failover-ttl-and-health-check). Async replication at 12 s p99 lag fits inside RPO 5 minutes; fencing revokes writes before promotion so the old primary cannot keep accepting them (r-database-replication-mode-and-promotion). S3 replication was enabled after the bucket had 1.2 M objects, so the Batch Replication job is cited (r-object-store-replication-verified). GitHub runners live only in the primary, so the failover script has a break-glass path from the secondary (r-region-scoped-dependencies-listed). The drill on 2026-08-20 is after the last mechanics change on 2026-07-14, so the decision is not labelled `unverified`; the one manual step is recorded for the next drill (r-drill-live-with-measured-results). Failback has its own RTO of 45 and a reconciliation step for writes taken in eu-central-1 (r-failback-procedure-included).

example.title: pilot light with zero data loss
example.note: What the validator prints: `dns.ttl_seconds` 3600 above the maximum of 60 (r-dns-failover-ttl-and-health-check); `database.fencing` and `single_writer_enforcement` are "n/a" (fm-03); the CI/CD dependency is unreachable with no `bypass` (r-region-scoped-dependencies-listed); cross-field: `achievable_rto_minutes` 90 above required 30 and `scale_up_minutes` 60 above RTO (r-pattern-chosen-from-rpo-rto-and-cost); `rpo_minutes` 0 with asynchronous replication at 40 s p99 lag (fm-01); `drill.last` null and `decision` not labelled `unverified` (fm-02). What the reviewer sees: "zero data loss" in the decision on top of async replication, an S3 bucket with no backfill and no backlog alert, and a failback that says "reverse the failover" (fm-05, r-failback-procedure-included).
